items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math
items.excerpt: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced an AI-generated (Claude-assisted) proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, long considered far out of reach for human mathematicians, capping AI's year-long run of math results.

history_match.title: Dueling proofs from OpenAI and Anthropic astound scientists

items.title: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is almost certainly true, independent mathematicians attest
items.excerpt: Independent mathematicians say they are near to completing verification of the claimed AI-assisted solution to the Riemann hypothesis and that it is almost certainly correct. Follow-up to the same-day announcement; curator should pick one Riemann item.

items.title: AI just solved the 'real' Navier-Stokes problem
items.excerpt: NYU's Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge claim a new AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup that closes the loophole critics found in OpenAI's September solution of the fluid-dynamics Millennium Prize problem.

history_match.title: The inside story behind OpenAI's million-dollar math proof

items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
items.excerpt: MIT LIDS researchers developed a physics-constrained machine learning approach that guarantees bounded predictions for chaotic systems, enabling reliable AI surrogates for turbulent flows, weather and climate modeling.

items.title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal-organic frameworks (MOFGen)
items.excerpt: MOFGen chains an LLM that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum-mechanical filter agents and synthesizability agents; it generated hundreds of thousands of MOFs and four 'AI-dreamt' MOFs were successfully synthesized. Off-list exception: no on-list outlet covered this materials result.

items.title: AI virtual cell technology could reveal how genetic changes and drugs alter cells
items.excerpt: Texas A&M's PertReason model predicts how genetic perturbations and drugs alter cell behavior and traces the biological pathways behind the change; its PertReasonQA benchmark checks whether LLMs reach right answers with the right evidence (arXiv, NeurIPS 2026).

history_match.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease

items.title: Scientists Use AI-Designed CRISPR to Make Disease-Resistant Rice
items.excerpt: University of Missouri's Bing Yang adapted Profluent's AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 editor for plants, knocking out three SWEET genes in rice with up to 97% efficiency; edited plants resisted three bacterial blight strains and passed edits to offspring.

history_match.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool

items.title: Adaptive AI agent connects experimental planning with robotic control in wastewater treatment test
items.excerpt: UCL and HKUST(GZ)'s Embodied Science Agent pairs a Bayesian-optimization planner with an adaptive robot; over 15 closed-loop rounds of dye-removal experiments it raised solution transmittance from 82% to 99.7% (arXiv preprint).

items.title: How AI can identify the magnetic structures behind high-frequency energy loss
items.excerpt: Tokyo University of Science used interpretable AI (persistent homology plus energy-landscape mapping) on micromagnetic simulations of an iron-based nanocrystalline soft magnet, pinpointing domain-wall features that raise the energy barrier as frequency climbs (NPG Asia Materials).

items.title: Noninvasive brain interface uses AI suggestions to convey messages nearly three times faster
items.excerpt: Rutgers researchers paired a noninvasive BCI with a locally run fine-tuned language model that suggests words and phrases; healthy participants spelled meaning-based messages nearly three times faster than with dictionary prediction (IEEE TBME).

items.title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations
items.excerpt: Penn State's PSUMamba fuses spectral, temporal and spatial hyperspectral data to flag crop stress before it is visible, reaching 94.47% accuracy on white button mushrooms with about ten times fewer operations than a Vision Transformer (Scientific Reports).

items.title: Researchers use AI to optimize sensor design for ultrasensitive vitamin C detection
items.excerpt: Sungkyunkwan University trained a machine learning model on 25 experiments to pick sensor-fabrication conditions out of 625 combinations; the AI-guided imprinted-polymer sensor hit a 778 pM detection limit and matched ELISA on urine samples (Chemical Engineering Journal).

items.title: Your Best Quantum Error Correction Engineer Might Be a Bot
items.excerpt: An analysis of how AI is taking an increasingly central role in designing new quantum error-correcting codes and decoders, from neural decoders to AI-searched code constructions.

history_match.title: Yonsei University Researchers Develop Mamba State-Space Neural Decoder to Enable Real-Time Quantum Error Correction

items.title: Sand grain-sized wireless chip can monitor reactions to provide data for self-driving labs
items.excerpt: A sand-grain-sized wireless sensor chip checks reaction temperature in real time, producing thousands of data points per hour to train the AI models that steer self-driving labs.

history_match.title: Researchers develop conversational AI for self-driving labs

items.title: Following the 'mathocalypse,' mathematicians consider the future
items.excerpt: At MIT, leading mathematicians discussed the quality of AI-generated math, how the 'mathocalypse' is challenging research norms, and what remains for mathematicians whether they embrace machines or stay 'AI vegans.'

items.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
items.excerpt: Researchers used AI to examine nearly 4,000 studies and hundreds of code repositories, finding gaps in the information needed to scrutinize and reuse published prediction research.

items.title: An Anthropic mathematician claims to have proven the Riemann hypothesis. We have to rethink how we reward expertise.
items.excerpt: Opinion: AI has upended the math community with a flood of results, and the field must rethink how it judges which questions and answers matter, putting humans back at the center. Same story as the SciAm Riemann items.

items.title: Catching AI's Mistakes Is a Mental Burden—and a Drag on Productivity
items.excerpt: A cognitive engineer explains the 'verification burden': productivity gains from AI are offset by the time and mental effort spent checking output, an instance of Woods' responsibility-authority double bind.
